A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VScan. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D are readable and matchable despite restructuring and additional experiments in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original VScan benchmark results, layerwise empirical studies, ablations, efficiency measurements and adversarial-subset evaluations in Sections 3–5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds benchmark evaluations, comparator results, training-cost measurements and expanded layerwise analysis.

M1.justification: The core global/local scanning, similarity-based merging and middle-layer pruning procedure remains unchanged. Appendix A5 newly sketches a multi-turn inference adaptation that reassesses and reselects query-relevant tokens for new questions. This is a limited proposed extension; the explicit averaging equation merely documents the existing merging rule.

E1.justification: Appendix A3 adds DocVQA, InfoVQA, MME-RealWorld, MM-Vet and MMMU, substantially extending coverage into document and infographic QA and additional multimodal evaluations. The original image, grounding, video and adversarial-subset coverage remains. Multi-turn conversations are discussed but not experimentally evaluated.

E2.justification: VisionZip joins the existing Qwen grounding comparisons in Table 4 and video comparisons in v3 Table 5, formerly v1 Table A1. New efficiency Table A4 compares FastV, PDrop and VisionZip with VScan. Figure 5 retains its original comparator set despite v3's prose mentioning VisionZip.

E3.justification: v3 adds a fine-tuning versus inference-only evaluation with an unpruned control in Table A3 and extends Study 3 to LLaVA-NeXT-7B. Existing pruning budgets, model-specific layer choices and evaluation metrics remain unchanged after matching v1 Appendix B2 to v3 Section 5.1. The new budget-accounting explanation does not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 4 adds LLaVA-NeXT-7B cases testing whether the layerwise convergence observation extends across models. Table A3 additionally examines whether applying pruning during fine-tuning improves retained accuracy over inference-only pruning. The original retention-rate, global/local mixture, local-layer and adversarial-subset analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, statistical error bars or significance tests. The layerwise prediction-confidence visualizations concern token probabilities rather than statistical uncertainty across experiments.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises SparseVLM's average retention scores at 192/128/64 tokens from 96.1/93.7/87.2% to 97.6/96.4/90.4%, while corresponding VScan scores remain unchanged. v3 adds results for five benchmarks, VisionZip comparisons, expanded convergence analysis and comparative efficiency. Table A3 newly reports training cost falling from 96 to 56 GPU hours with 96.7% performance retention over its five evaluated benchmarks.

T1.justification: No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical assumption is introduced. v3's explicit mean-merging equation and hidden-state projection formula restate operations already described in v1. The FLOPs expression is unchanged apart from numbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same empirically motivated, two-stage, training-free contribution and headline 2.91× prefill speedup, approximately 10× FLOPs reduction and 95.4% retained-performance claims. Additional experiments do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 expands the semantic-saturation explanation for middle-layer pruning, explains risks of imbalanced pruning stages, discusses multi-turn overhead, and qualifies comparisons involving borrowed final-token rather than average-token budgets. The efficiency–accuracy limitation added to the conclusion already appeared in v1 Appendix D.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a code-repository link and adds explanations of KV-cache compatibility, average-versus-final token accounting, and Study 3's logit extraction. These improve documentation without establishing changed implementations. Much of Section 5.1's fuller detail already existed in v1 Appendix B2; the new fine-tuning experiment still lacks a complete reproduction recipe.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to AuroraCap, DocVQA, InfographicVQA and Video-MMLU, while removing the GPT-4 report, Not all patches are what you need, and MLVU. The text-agnostic/text-aware positioning remains unchanged. Publication and title updates for existing methods are not treated as new related work.

P1.justification: Most central prose is retained, with localized explanatory expansions. Detailed settings and video results move into the main text, appendices are reorganized, and author and publication information changes. The overall introduction–analysis–method–experiments narrative remains stable.

P2.justification: Figure 4 gains a second model panel, grounding and video tables gain comparator rows, and seven appendix result tables are introduced. Tables A5–A7 tabulate the existing Figure 5 results rather than representing new experiments. The video table moves into the main text, and TMLR typography, spacing and headers substantially reformat the document.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens validation through document and infographic tests, additional VisionZip comparisons, and direct baseline efficiency measurements, while improving access and protocol documentation. These gains are tempered by missing fine-tuning setup details and the unsupported inclusion of VisionZip in the Figure 5 discussion. The evidence supports a positive but limited overall quality improvement.
